original_draft: Pure water at standard atmospheric pressure freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius. At high altitude the air pressure is not lower, so water boils at a lower temperature; on the summit of Mount Everest it boils at roughly 70 degrees Celsius. Liquid water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius. Ice is less dense than liquid water, which is why it floats and why lakes freeze from the top down. A water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom, and the molecule is bent rather than straight. Water covers about 71 percent of Earth's surface, and most of it is salt water in the oceans.
